subject: Cloud Computing
title: The Staffing Cost of Cloud
description: A fast breakdown of The Staffing Cost of Cloud for builders.

hook.text: Cloud engineers earn $150,000+ per year. The cloud promised to reduce IT costs — but salaries keep rising.

buildup.text: Cloud didn't eliminate IT jobs. It changed them. You need architects, DevOps engineers, and security specialists.

discovery.text: Companies that migrate to cloud without training their teams end up hiring expensive consultants instead.

twist.text: The cloud skills gap is real. Demand for cloud engineers far exceeds supply, driving salaries even higher.

climax.text: Cloud infrastructure is cheaper. Cloud talent is not. Staffing is often the largest hidden cost of cloud adoption.

punchline.text: Cloud saves on hardware. It spends on people.

quiz.question: Why is staffing often the largest hidden cost of cloud adoption?
options: Cloud requires specialized engineers whose salaries far exceed traditional IT roles
Cloud providers require companies to hire their certified staff
Cloud systems need 10 times more staff than on-premises

details.summary: Cloud engineering salaries are among the highest in IT, and demand consistently outstrips supply. The staffing cost to build, operate, and optimize cloud infrastructure often exceeds the cloud bill itself. Managed services reduce staffing needs at the cost of higher service prices.
details.whyItMatters: Many organizations compare only cloud service prices and forget that skilled cloud engineers cost $150,000 to $300,000 or more annually. Staffing is often the largest real cost of cloud adoption.
takeaways: Cloud engineer salaries often exceed the cloud bill itself
Managed services reduce staffing needs at higher service costs
Training existing staff is cheaper than hiring cloud specialists

faq.question: How many cloud engineers does a company need?
faq.answer: A rough guide is one platform engineer per 10 to 20 application developers for organizations with significant cloud usage. Smaller companies can rely more on managed services. Larger enterprises need dedicated teams for security, networking, and cost optimization.

faq.question: Can managed services replace cloud engineers?
faq.answer: Partially. Managed services eliminate operational tasks like patching and backup. But someone still needs to architect solutions, configure services, manage costs, and respond to incidents. Managed services shift the role from operations to architecture and optimization.
